subject: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?

messages.author: 7c852a2f0f62047b
messages.subject: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
parts:
Hi!
I'm trying to create detection histories with each occasion or survey being a specific month. If I set occasionlength=30 or 31 my data will slowly shift out of the month windows. Is there a way or a work around to make this happen?
thanks, 
-Rachel

messages.author: 6c32846711f6e460
messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
parts:
Because months aren't all the same length, and because camtrapR only works with occasion lengths in days, you can't do this as far as I know. If you really wanted to you could collapse the detection histories manually e.g. renaming o1, o2 ... o(n) with dates and collapsing through a pivot table for example; however, your data won't be standardised, either, as you'd have varying numbers of days that make up each detection history block, so you'd probably want standardise the number of days e.g. omitting the 31st day (or, if you're surveying in February, omitting the 29th, 30th, 31st ... unless you're working in a leap year ... ). Long story short, camtrapR only allows occasion lengths in "days", not hours, months, years, so if you want to do this you'll have to do it manually. Weeks simply work better because no matter what time of year, a week always has 7 days, whereas months are just a bit of a pain.

Jarrad

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
parts:
Hi Rachel,
like Jarred said, occasion lengths equal to specific months is currently not implemented in camtrapR. If I find the time I might try to implement this in a coming release. But for now it is not available.

A workaround would be to format date/time in the record table as year-month, create an empty detection history (Station x month) with all 0, then for each station write a 1 into the cells of the detection matrix for every month with a record. I currently don't have any code available for this operation. 
This workaround would also not account for varying effort due to the number of days per month (as Jarred pointed out) and also incompletely sampled months (due to setup and retrieval days not on the 1st/last day of the month). As a consequence, your results might be off when effort is not taken into account.

Does anyone else miss this feature? The more interest there is, the sooner I'll address it.
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
parts:
Hi Rachel,
Here is a possible workaround. The idea is to create separate detection histories with different occasion lengths for each month, then combine them all into one. For every month, change 2 arguments: occasionLength and day1.

Some caveats here: 
- in the first month, set day1 to the day the first camera was set up, and set occasionLength so that the occasion ends on the last day of the month (check column names in resulting detection history)
- the  proposed workaround only works if there is at least one record at any station in a given month. Otherwise, there will be an error to avoid returning an empty detection history (this is why below i added a record manually)
- I would have liked to include the argument maxNumberDays in detectionHistory, but that didn't work due to a bug. I'll investigate and update when I know more.
- if your study covered many months, you might wish to automate this using e.g. a for loop. 


Here's a example based on the sample data in the package. 


# load station information
data(camtraps)

# create camera operation matrix
camop_no_problem <- cameraOperation(CTtable      = camtraps,
                                    stationCol   = "Station",
                                    setupCol     = "Setup_date",
                                    retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",
                                    hasProblems  = FALSE,
                                    dateFormat   = "%d/%m/%Y"
)

data(recordTableSample)    # load the record history, as created above

# add a record in May, so function doesn't fail

rowToAdd <- recordTableSample[5,]
rowToAdd$DateTimeOriginal <- "2009-05-10 05:07:00"   # add 1 month to the date
recordTableSample <- rbind(recordTableSample,
                           rowToAdd)
      

# Detection history April
DetHist_2009_04 <- detectionHistory(recordTable         = recordTableSample,
                             camOp                = camop_no_problem,
                             stationCol           = "Station",
                             speciesCol           = "Species",
                             recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTimeOriginal",
                             species              = "VTA",
                             occasionLength       = 29,
                             day1                 = "2009-04-02",
                             datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,
                             includeEffort        = TRUE,
                             scaleEffort          = FALSE,
                             timeZone             = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"
)

# Detection history May
DetHist_2009_05 <- detectionHistory(recordTable          = recordTableSample,
                                    camOp                = camop_no_problem,
                                    stationCol           = "Station",
                                    speciesCol           = "Species",
                                    recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTimeOriginal",
                                    species              = "VTA",
                                    occasionLength       = 31,
                                    day1                 = "2009-05-01",
                                    datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,
                                    includeEffort        = TRUE,
                                    scaleEffort          = FALSE,
                                    timeZone             = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"
)

DetHist_2009_04
DetHist_2009_05

# make list of detection histories and effort matrices
DetHistList <- list(DetHist_2009_04$detection_history,
                    DetHist_2009_05$detection_history)
EffortList <- list(DetHist_2009_04$effort,
                   DetHist_2009_05$effort)

# take the first column of each, preserving proper column and row names
DetHist_tmp <- lapply(DetHistList, FUN = function(x) {
  y <- matrix(x[, 1], ncol = 1)
  colnames(y) <- colnames(x)[1]
  rownames(y) <- rownames(x)
  data.frame(y, check.names = FALSE)
  y
  })

Effort_tmp <- lapply(EffortList, FUN = function(x) {
  y <- matrix(x[, 1], ncol = 1)
  colnames(y) <- colnames(x)[1]
  rownames(y) <- rownames(x)
  data.frame(y, check.names = FALSE)
  y
  })

# combine into single data frame
dethist_combined <- do.call(cbind, DetHist_tmp)
effort_combined  <- do.call(cbind, Effort_tmp)

# check results
dethist_combined
effort_combined
